summary.headline: Capri Global posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of Rs 418 crore (+77% YoY), but gold loan Stage-2 rose Rs 1,266 crore on technical delinquencies.
summary.overview: Consolidated AUM reached Rs 43,878 crore (+62% YoY, +9% QoQ) with gold loans, MSME, housing and construction finance all growing. Net interest income rose 69% YoY to Rs 812 crore and cost-to-income improved to 41-42.6%. Asset quality weakened in gold loans: Stage-2 rose Rs 1,266 crore and consolidated gross Stage-3 rose 22 bps QoQ to 1.2%, which management attributes to shorter-tenure repayment products introduced after RBI's April 2026 gold loan rules. Management maintained FY27 AUM guidance of about Rs 50,000 crore and PAT of about Rs 1,600 crore, and reiterated a Rs 65,000 crore AUM target for FY28.

financial_highlights.change: from 44% in Q1 FY27 and 49% in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Blended yield / spread on net advances

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 21,000 crore (+10% QoQ, +102% YoY); 1,154 gold branches, AUM per branch Rs 18.2 crore (vs Rs 19.2 crore); yield 19%; Stage-2 up Rs 1,266 crore, entirely gold, and gross Stage-3 up Rs 126 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 7,016 crore (+25% YoY); Q2 disbursement Rs 560 crore (+36% YoY); GNPA about 3.1%, stable over the last 3-4 quarters; Micro-LAP AUM Rs 929 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 8,325 crore (+39% YoY); GNPA 1.2%, Stage-3 steady at 1.2%; expansion planned in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: Construction finance
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 7,503 crore (+51% YoY) across 304 projects; Stage-3 fell to 0.02% after Rs 45 crore write-offs and about Rs 9 crore recoveries.

segments.name: Co-lending and DA
segments.commentary: Co-lending AUM Rs 9,083 crore (+60% YoY, +12% QoQ), 21% of AUM; direct assignment now 28% of co-lending AUM; co-lending and DA income Rs 72 crore (+11% QoQ).

segments.name: Insurance distribution and car loans
segments.commentary: Insurance net fee income Rs 51 crore in Q2; car loan originations Rs 3,601 crore (+27% YoY) across 13 partner banks and 821 locations.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM guidance maintained at about Rs 50,000 crore; management said it may slightly exceed this.
FY27 PAT expected at about Rs 1,600 crore.
FY28 targets: AUM Rs 65,000 crore, ROAE about 20-21% (about 19-21% in closing remarks), ROAA 4.2-4.7%.
Credit cost sustainably in the 0.6-0.9% range.
Branch additions: board approval for 600 branches this year, about 500 in gold loans; year-end branch count about 1,500 (gold-loan-focused), versus 1,609 total branches at September 2026.
Gold loan Stage-2 expected to fall significantly by end of Q3 FY27 after discontinuing short-tenure schemes.
Proposed IRDAI distribution rules: ROAE for FY28 and FY29 may fall about 1% at consolidated level; FY27 impact seen as limited.
capex_capacity: Branch network 1,609 at end-September 2026 after net addition of 176 (154 gold, 22 non-gold); 1,154 gold branches.
More than 86% of gold branches are already profitable; branches older than 18 months average about Rs 20 crore AUM; new branches expected at Rs 4-7 crore AUM.
Gold collateral in custody rose to 21 tons (+28% YoY, +4% QoQ); 8 lakh gold loan customers referenced.
Employee count rose by 1,477 in Q2; gold loan employee productivity Rs 3.4 crore (vs Rs 1.8 crore a year earlier).
Technology: Sentinel underwriting platform, Pegasus and Kronos collections platforms, agentic AI and in-house decisioning targeting millisecond latency; OpenAI partnership being institutionalised.
demand_pricing: Gold loan yield rose to 19% in Q2 FY27 as ticket sizes stayed below Rs 3 lakh and teaser loans were reduced; management said yields should hold despite competitor pricing pressure.
Average gold loan ticket size reached about Rs 2.14 lakh, with LTV on fresh disbursements at 73.8%; portfolio LTV about 70%+.
Vyapar Mela campaign used short-window low-rate offers, with smaller-ticket customers kept at original rates.
Co-lending transition to new CLA rules: over half of partner banks have moved; income now recognised over contract life rather than upfront.
Customer base exceeds 8 lakh; live unique customers rose to 7,13,000 from 7,00,659.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company defend gold loan yields against peers cutting rates, especially in the South?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields rose to 19% by focusing on sub-Rs 5 lakh tickets and shorter-tenure teaser loans, and expects yields not to fall significantly, preferring to grow in smaller tickets rather than at lower yields.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost of funds rise, given about 70% of borrowings are bank term loans with MCLR resets?
qa_highlights.answer: No material pressure yet, as spreads were cut with several banks; MCLR resets could add about 15-20 bps. Management plans to offset this with more short-tenure CP and NCD borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and net NPA rise sharply QoQ, and where did slippages occur?
qa_highlights.answer: Slippages were confined to gold loans, from shorter-tenure (1-3 month) products; management expects Stage-2 to fall substantially by end of next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance being revised after strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM guidance kept at about Rs 50,000 crore (already about Rs 44,000 crore), and PAT expected at about Rs 1,600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new co-lending guidelines on income?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending income can no longer be booked upfront and is recognised over contract life; capital is released by downselling, so management says earning potential is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Stage-3 provision coverage fall from 43.2% to 33.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited segment PCRs: MSME about 45%, housing about 38%, construction finance about 50%, gold loans about 19%, which it considers adequate given collateral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effect of the drought and gold price correction on the portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought stress seen only in some semi-urban and rural gold branches; MSME, housing and construction finance show no impact. Management said a 5-7% gold price correction is absorbed by the about 30% LTV cushion.

risks_watch: Gold loan Stage-2 (+Rs 1,266 crore QoQ) and gross Stage-3 at 1.2%; the company expects reversal by Q3 FY27, which needs confirmation.
PCR on Stage-3 fell to 33.3% (from 43.2%); gold loan PCR is about 19%.
Cost of funds could rise by 15-20 bps as MCLR resets, with about 70% of borrowings from banks.
Gold loan AUM per branch fell to Rs 18.2 crore as branch additions outpace maturity; new branches are at Rs 4-7 crore.
Drought stress in rural gold branches and gold price volatility; collateral LTV rules changes.
Proposed IRDAI distribution rules could cut FY28-29 ROAE by about 1%; co-lending income recognition is shifting to over the contract life.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and FY27-28 targets, and explicit that gold loan delinquencies are temporary and technical. Less specific on the sharp drop in gold PCR and on the timing of the cost-of-funds impact.
key_quotes: Capri Global delivers strong quarterly performance in Q2 FY '27, continuing its growth momentum and maintaining asset quality while delivering highest ever quarterly profit of Rs. 418 crores, a 77% increase year-on-year.

The increase in reported GNPA in gold loan particularly reflects product-level repayment dynamics and our calibrated approach to collateral enforcement rather than a corresponding increase in expected credit losses.
So, by end of the next quarter, you will see delinquency coming down significantly in the gold loan segment.

adds.what: About 500 gold-loan branches (600 non-gold and gold total approved by board this year); year-end branch count about 1,500 vs 1,609 at September 2026

growth.why: FY27 AUM guided at about Rs 50,000 crore (held, may slightly exceed) and PAT about Rs 1,600 crore, with FY28 AUM target Rs 65,000 crore; backing is partly specific (600 branches approved, ~500 gold, AUM 43,878 crore, +62% YoY) but no concrete capex or timeline for FY28 growth, and year-end branch count guided down to ~1,500 from 1,609.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Yield rose to 19% on gold and spread to 8.3% on net advances with cost-to-income down to 41% from 49% a year ago, but MCLR resets could add 15-20 bps to cost of funds with about 70% of borrowings from banks.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Board approved 600 branches this year (about 500 gold), yet the year-end count is guided to about 1,500 vs 1,609 at September 2026, so net branch count is set to fall while gold branches stay the growth vehicle.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM Rs 43,878 crore (+62% YoY, +9% QoQ) and FY27 AUM guidance of about Rs 50,000 crore is held and may be slightly exceeded, implying roughly Rs 6,000 crore more in the second half.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board already approved 600 branches and housing expansion into Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh is planned, but no new capital programme was discussed beyond the branch rollout.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 AUM and PAT guidance (Rs 50,000 crore and about Rs 1,600 crore) were held rather than raised despite H1 PAT of Rs 772 crore, and AUM is already about Rs 44,000 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gold Stage-2 rose Rs 1,266 crore, gross Stage-3 is 1.2% (+22 bps QoQ), and PCR on Stage-3 fell to 33.3% from 43.2%; the expected Q3 FY27 reversal is not yet confirmed.

rows.label: IRDAI distribution rules could cut FY28-29 ROAE
rows.why: Management sees consolidated ROAE for FY28 and FY29 falling about 1% under the proposed rules, with FY27 impact limited.

rows.label: Gold Stage-2 reversal by Q3 FY27
rows.why: Management expects Stage-2 to fall significantly after discontinuing short-tenure schemes, from the Rs 1,266 crore QoQ rise, but this is not yet confirmed.

rows.label: Gold loan yield defence at 19%
rows.why: Yield rose to 19% with tickets below Rs 3 lakh, and management expects yields to hold despite peer rate cuts, though MCLR resets could add 15-20 bps to funding costs.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM, PAT and FY28 targets and called gold delinquencies technical, but analysts pressed on the Stage-2 rise, the drop in Stage-3 provision coverage, and cost-of-funds timing; management was less specific on both.
